why: The v0.7.0 release run was cancelled by its own 20-minute budget and the release shipped without provenance (D-196). Re-measured for the v0.12.0 cut because the suite materially grew again: the outline-arc (#228), footprint-copper-graphic (#230), live-probe (#234), benchmark-replay (#235), root-zone-census (#236) and multi-pin routing (#237, #238) arc took it from 3,583 tests at the v0.11.0 boundary to 3,799 collected. No budget is raised by this re-record. Every ceiling still clears the half rule -- but the ci.yml:test margin has narrowed sharply and this is the first boundary at which that is the headline rather than a footnote: the worst leg moved from 2,332s to 3,302s (+41.6%), which is 91.7% of the way to the 3,600s half-rule limit on the 120-minute ceiling. A further ~9% growth in the worst leg breaches the rule. The two lanes open at this cut (feat/live-version-binding and the multi-pin repair hardening on PR #239) are not in this release and will land under a fresh Unreleased; whichever release wave takes them must re-measure this job first and expect to confront the ceiling rather than re-record past it.
source: GitHub Actions REST API, read-only: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs/{run_id}/jobs and GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/jobs/{job_id}. `seconds` is completed_at - started_at for the hosted job, including runner setup, checkout and post-steps -- the same wall clock bounded by job-level `timeout-minutes`.
half_rule: A budget must be at least twice the longest recorded duration of the job it bounds. Equivalently, when a measured gate exceeds half of an explicit timeout budget, raise or re-measure that budget before release.
update: Re-record before raising or lowering any budget and before every release wave that materially grows the suite. Use only completed jobs whose GitHub conclusion is exactly `success`; failed and cancelled runs stop early and therefore do not measure the work. Replace the affected job's observations with the newest representative successful sample, then run `python scripts/check_ci_budgets.py`.
conclusion: Every observation below records conclusion `success`. No failed, skipped or cancelled job is used for calibration.
not_claimed: This is a small operational sample, not a latency distribution or percentile estimate. The half-rule margin, rather than an inferred percentile, separates the observed maximum from the declared ceiling.

jobs.note: The two newest successful ci.yml runs at the v0.12.0 release boundary, both post-merge `main` pushes: the multi-pin branch-repair tip (63de4c3, #238) and the multi-pin lattice merge (30ef71f, #237). All three Python matrix legs of each are recorded because they share one job-level budget. The worst leg is Python 3.12 at 3302s (55.03 min), against 2332s (38.87 min) at the v0.11.0 boundary -- a 41.6% increase in one wave, and the largest single-boundary jump this file has recorded. It still clears the half rule (110.07 min needed against a 120-minute ceiling) but with only 9.93 minutes of headroom. This job, not release.yml:verify, is now the longest duration recorded anywhere in this file; that changed at this boundary.

The latest completed release workflow, v0.11.0, replacing the v0.10.0 sample recorded at the previous boundary. Its release gate ran to completion and the job conclusion was success. 2325s (38.75 min) against v0.10.0's 2374s (39.57 min) -- this job got very slightly faster while ci.yml:test grew by 41.6%, because the hosted release gate skips the real-KiCad nodes the matrix legs run. It is no longer the longest duration in this file.
